properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14.

═══ ⭐⭐ ADDED 2026-08-14 (LATER, SAME DAY): HIS INHERITANCE-VERSUS-COMPOSITION FRAMING, WHICH CUTS AGAINST DEPTH AND IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT ON THIS NODE ═══

HIS WORDS: *"it reminds me [of] a python class that inherits another class that inherits another class and on (depth). this is different from composition architectures where there is no inheritance and everything is horizontal. In [that] case, is it good that reflow2 is horizontal or would there be some advantages in making things have some level of depth?"*

⇒ **THE ANALOGY IMPORTS A SETTLED ENGINEERING ARGUMENT, AND IT ARGUES FOR THE SHAPE REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS.** "Prefer composition over inheritance" is doctrine because deep hierarchies are rigid: the taxonomy has to be right before the work is understood, a change to a base ripples to every descendant, and the ladder is expensive to re-cut once things hang off it. **On that reading reflow2's flat shape is not a deficiency to be corrected but the safer default**, and the burden falls on anyone proposing depth to say what it BUYS.

⚠️ **BUT THE ANALOGY IS IMPERFECT IN ONE SPECIFIC WAY, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LOAD-BEARING.** In code, inheritance and composition are ALTERNATIVES — two ways to reuse behaviour, and picking one excludes the other. In this graph they are NOT alternatives, because they answer different questions: `CONTAINS` says *what is this made of*, `DEPENDS_ON` says *what does this need*, and a design legitimately has both at once. So "horizontal versus vertical" is not the same trade as "composition versus inheritance", and reading it as one would make depth look like a competing architecture when it is an orthogonal axis.

⭐ **WHERE THE ANALOGY DOES BITE, EXACTLY: `DECOMPOSES`.** That edge is the one relation here that behaves like inheritance — a child decomposes a parent and **delivery ROLLS UP**, so satisfying every child satisfies the parent. That is a base-class contract with arithmetic attached, and it is brittle in precisely the way deep inheritance is. **AND THE COST IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL — IT WAS PRICED THE SAME DAY:** `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` → `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` (built 2026-08-14, PR #181) exists because the roll-up never checks that the children AMOUNT TO the parent, so a requirement split into two children addressing a tenth of it reports `delivered` the moment both close. **Depth buys computable roll-up and costs the risk that the roll-up lies.** That is the trade, stated in one line, and it did not exist on this node before he raised the analogy.

📌 SO THE QUESTION IS NARROWED, NOT ANSWERED: not *"should the design be deeper?"* but **"which of the three depth ladders earns its brittleness?"** — and each is separable. `CONTAINS` (assembly) is cheap and carries no arithmetic. `DECOMPOSES` (requirement roll-up) is the expensive one and now has its counterweight built. `Component.level` / `Capability.tier` are labels that compute almost nothing today.

═══ 🛑 RE-MEASURED 2026-08-14 AFTER HIS QUESTION — AND A THIRD UNUSED LADDER APPEARS ═══
```
DECOMPOSES ................ 0        (requirement lineage: original 164, decomposed 0, derived 0)
Component.level ........... component 48 · subsystem 8 · system 0 · SoS 0 · enterprise 0
Capability.tier ........... operational 147 · UNSET 14 · strategic 0 · tactical 0   <- NEW
Component CONTAINS ........ 42 edges over 8 parents (of 56 components)
lateral ................... DEPENDS_ON 178 · ALLOCATED_TO 178 · SATISFIES 192
PART_OF_FLOW .............. 0   (zero Flow nodes)
```
⚠️ **`Capability.tier` WAS NOT ON THIS NODE BEFORE AND IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE: 147 of 161 capabilities carry `operational` and NOTHING carries `strategic` or `tactical`.** A three-value ladder holding one value is not a shallow hierarchy, it is an unused field — and it is the SAME vocabulary Alex's tier request (`dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`) would reach for. **Measured separately the same day: `Capability.tier` carries no schema description at all**, so nothing tells an agent what it means or how it relates to `Component.level`. Three ladders exist, and all three are close to empty.

⇒ **THE HONEST READING OF ALL THREE NUMBERS: reflow2's design is not flat because someone weighed depth and chose against it. It is flat because the depth vocabulary was never filled in.** That is a different fact from "horizontal is right here", and it means the composition-versus-inheritance question **cannot be settled from this design's shape** — the evidence is absence of modelling, not evidence of a considered choice. Which is exactly what option (b) below already warned it would be measuring.

════════════ THE ORIGINAL CAPTURE, 2026-08-14 ════════════

HIS WORDS: *"I almost want 'missing the wood for the trees' to be a skill of reflow2. that sometimes somebody becomes so wrapped up in some little detail that they forget the big picture… another way to look at it is 'breadth' vs 'depth' of a design… you can probably error in going too far in one dimension without considering the other dimension - need to find the correct balance. not sure if there is a way to measure in a graph depth vs breadth? if it can be measured, then there probably becomes a ratio of depth-to-breadth that is ideal to maintain. maybe in a graph you can count all the nodes (peer to peer nodes and this is your horizontal score). then count all the components nodes that make up a system (kind of looking at system-of-systems to systems to components and so on) and this is your depth score."*

═══ ✅ YES, IT IS MEASURABLE, AND HIS PROPOSED SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE ═══

Run on reflow2's own export (`c18a4a1`, 2026-08-14):
```
DEPTH                                   BREADTH
  Components ................ 56          lateral edges ........... 203
  component CONTAINS ........ 42            DEPENDS_ON 178 · CONSUMES 15
  MAX NESTING DEPTH ......... 2             PROVIDES 6 · INTERACTS_WITH 4
  components with no parent . 14          hierarchical edges ...... 122 CONTAINS
  DECOMPOSES edges .......... 0                                     + 0 DECOMPOSES
  Component.level used: component 48, subsystem 8
                        system 0, system_of_systems 0, enterprise 0
  Requirements 164 · Capabilities 161, all at one level
```

🛑 **REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN IS ALMOST PURE BREADTH.** 164 requirements with **zero** decomposition; 56 components nested at most **two** deep, using two of five `level` values; 14 components parented by nothing. **The project built around `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` — *"nested as deep as the design needs"*, which Anthony called *"one of the primary things I designed it for"* — has a flat design.**

═══ ⚠️ A CORRECTION MADE BEFORE THIS NODE WAS SAVED, AND IT MATTERS ═══

This session first wrote that the blind spot had **doubled from 6 to 14** since 2026-08-07. **That was wrong.** `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` already recorded BOTH numbers on the same day — `components_outside_any_subsystem: 6` and `component_roots: 14` — as two different measures, not a before and after. **The truth is less dramatic and arguably worse: the numbers are IDENTICAL a week later.** `hierarchy_issues` 0, roots 14, max_depth 2, `DECOMPOSES` 0 — a fully measured defect, unchanged.
📌 The error was caught by the near-duplicate guard surfacing that node — the same guard this session has documented firing wrongly seven times today. **Here it was right, and it prevented a false claim entering the record.**

═══ WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW HERE, beyond the 2026-08-07 measurement ═══

  · `Component.level` uses **two of five** values — nothing is a `system`, `system_of_systems` or `enterprise`. The ladder his idea depends on is three-fifths unused.
  · **Lateral 203 vs hierarchical 122** — the breadth/depth contrast stated as a single comparison, which is his proposed metric and which nothing computes today.
  · `DEPENDS_ON` has grown 171 → 178 in the week while `DECOMPOSES` stayed at 0. **The design is getting wider and no deeper**, which is the trend his idea is for and which no report shows.
  · 📌 **IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE FOR WORK ACCEPTED EARLIER TODAY:** `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` is planned to ask whether a decomposition's children cover their parent. **With 0 `DECOMPOSES` edges it cannot be dogfooded on this graph at all** — it would ship doing nothing here and nobody would notice. Not an argument against building it; an argument for testing it elsewhere. (BUILT 2026-08-14, PR #181, and it shipped saying exactly this about itself.)

═══ ⚠️ THE "IDEAL RATIO" IS THE OVERFIT THIS IDEA EXISTS TO PREVENT ═══

**A depth-to-breadth target derived from any one design is exactly the specialisation Anthony warned against in the same message.** A house, a beamline, a shop and an MCP server share no natural proportion, and `req:design-anything` forbids binding the tool to one discipline's habits. Two recorded failures agree:
  · `evaluate_allocation` reports **modularity 1.0 from `total_internal: 1, total_external: 0`** — a perfect score over ONE dependency while the graph holds 178 `DEPENDS_ON` edges. **A ratio over a starved denominator is that failure again.**
  · BL-5's lesson, in `detect.rs`: **a loud detector needs a different QUESTION, not a tuned number.**

⭐⭐ **THE ANTIDOTE IS ALREADY BUILT: `granularity_report`.** It answers a structurally identical question — *is the build coarser than the design?* — and its contract says *"IT NEVER SAYS 'monolith', 'too big' or 'split it', carries NO severity… THERE IS NO SIZE THRESHOLD: artifacts are compared against THIS DESIGN'S OWN DISTRIBUTION."* ⇒ **A breadth/depth measure should report the numbers and the design's own distribution, name what it cannot see, and refuse a verdict.** No universal ideal, no target, no severity. `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` reaches the same conclusion from the other side: *"what is wrong is a metric reporting a value at all when its denominator is one, instead of saying it has too little to measure."*

═══ AND ON THE SKILL ITSELF ═══

⚠️ **A SKILL ALONE REPEATS A FAILURE THIS PROJECT HAS MEASURED REPEATEDLY.** "Step back and look at the whole" is exactly what a session under load stops doing; `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` exists because an agent keeps adding nodes while the loop silently stops, and `dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types` settled that the manual trigger is the only one not depending on the mechanism that keeps failing. **A wood-for-trees skill nobody remembers to invoke is the joke telling itself.**

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **A USER-TYPED SKILL, NO METRIC.** Cheap, reliable trigger (human). Counter: tells the user little they did not already suspect when they typed it.
(b) ⭐ **MEASURE + SKILL, ON `granularity_report`'s NO-THRESHOLD SHAPE** — report depth, breadth and this design's own distribution; refuse a verdict; the skill puts the question. Counter: needs an honest answer to *what counts as depth* while `DECOMPOSES` is unused and `Component.level` is three-fifths empty — today it would mostly be reporting **absence of modelling** rather than a property of the system. ⭐ **THE RE-MEASUREMENT ABOVE STRENGTHENS THIS COUNTER: with `Capability.tier` also one-valued, ALL THREE depth ladders are near-empty, so a measure shipped today would report unfilled fields in three places and call it shape.**
(c) **A RATIO WITH A TARGET.** Argued against above on this node's own evidence.
(d) **NOTHING — `where-am-i` re-orients already.** Counter: it reports what the design SAYS and has no notion of proportion; it surfaced none of the numbers above.

📌 THE HONEST OPEN QUESTION UNDER ALL OF IT: is reflow2's flat shape a DEFECT, or a correct reading of a system that genuinely has 56 peer components and little natural hierarchy? **The measure cannot answer that and must not pretend to** — which is why `granularity_report` refuses a verdict, and why this stays a question rather than becoming a check. ⚠️ **AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT NARROWS EVEN THAT: with three ladders unfilled, the flatness is at least partly unmodelled rather than observed, so this design cannot be the evidence either way.**
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 measure a design's BREADTH against its DEPTH and prompt a step back? It is measurable, reflow2's own design is nearly all breadth, and an "ideal ratio" would be the overfit the idea exists to prevent
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill and measured on reflow2's own export before anything was written, because the central question — can depth and breadth be counted — is answerable rather than arguable. The measurement confirmed his proposed shape works and showed this design is nearly all breadth despite being built around recursive decomposition. A wrong claim is recorded in the node rather than quietly dropped: this session asserted the unparented-component count had doubled, and the prior fact node showed both figures were taken the same day, so the real finding is that a fully measured defect is unchanged a week later. The "ideal ratio" half is argued against rather than deferred, since a target derived from one design is the specialisation he raised the idea to avoid, and `granularity_report` already demonstrates the correct pattern — report the distribution, name what cannot be seen, refuse the verdict.
